svg.style: background:#0d1117; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif;
svg.text: Agentic Runtime Security — Alternative Architecture (Bedrock AgentCore)
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore + HashiCorp Vault Enterprise — dynamic credentials & user attribution with no self-managed cluster, no IVIA / OpenLDAP
IdP is pluggable — IVIA is now
managed, serverless agent runtime + agent identity — no EKS, no ServiceAccounts, no NetworkPolicy to operate
Each agent = a unique, centrally managed identity (ARN)
workload identity for agents + user-context JWT issuance
Replaces Vault K8s auth + IVIA as the token issuer
each agent = a Vault identity entity
creds die with the JWT lease
agent id + user id + JWT + lease
outside the runtime — reached only with Vault-vended, short-lived JIT credentials
One audit stream — Vault's tamper-evident log, no extra instrumentation
agent identity · resolved user identity (JWT claims)
JWT metadata · credential lease ID · timestamp
Which user caused this database query?
access data with scoped JIT creds
What changes vs. the IVIA + Vault reference
IVIA + OpenLDAP (on EKS) → AgentCore Identity + external OIDC IdP
Self-managed EKS agent pods → AgentCore Runtime (managed, serverless)
Vault Kubernetes auth → AgentCore workload identity (JWT)
CIBA out-of-band consent → AgentCore Secure Token Vault (OBO)
Unchanged: Vault Agent Registry · ephemeral authz · dynamic secrets · audit
AWS-only (AgentCore not multi-cloud). Vault native AI-agent support = beta (Ent 2.0.3+).
Each system still owns exactly one trust plane; the seam is now Vault ↔ AgentCore JWKS.
